ops.title: cc-pool — daemonkit migration (Waves 1-2)
ops.body:
cc-pool's daemon lifecycle runs on daemonkit as of commit `4e1050a` ("migrate onto daemonkit v0.1.0 — import flip, takeover, drain"), Waves 1 and 2 of the migration. daemonkit owns the mechanism (detached spawn, single-entrant socket bind, the takeover ladder, the drain state machine, the dev/release version taxonomy); cc-pool keeps the policy and its frozen JSON socket protocol. Five behaviors changed.

## Version stamping: consumer-owned vars, daemonkit taxonomy

`internal/version/version.go:9#cj8e` keeps the ldflags-injected `Version`/`Commit` in cc-pool's own package. Release and CI builds inject `-X github.com/yasyf/cc-pool/internal/version.Version=...` (`.github/workflows/release.yml:65#vftk`, `.github/formula/cc-pool.rb.tmpl:69#nkye`). `version.String()` resolves through `daemonkit/version`: a stamped release passes through unchanged with Commit appended, and an unstamped `"dev"` build resolves to daemonkit's `DevString` keyed on the executable's mtime. That ordering is load-bearing for takeover: a freshly rebuilt dev daemon compares strictly newer than the older running one, so it can evict it. The vars are consumer-owned: point ldflags at cc-pool's `internal/version`, never at daemonkit's version package.

## Takeover: newer-wins, protocol-skew-tolerant

`listen` binds the socket through `proc.SingleEntrant` (`internal/daemon/server.go:457#a29t`); its `Evict` closure runs `daemon.Run` with `Contract: daemon.RequestDaemon` and `WaitMode: daemon.SocketRelease` (`internal/daemon/server.go:461#cmkr`). Two outcomes matter:

- `Bind` — the socket is clear, or a strictly-older incumbent was evicted via the Shutdown, then grace, then SIGKILL ladder. The SIGKILL is PID-revalidated: `socketPeerPID` reads the kernel-attested socket owner via `getsockopt(LOCAL_PEERPID)` (`internal/daemon/peer.go:16#thrm`), so the kill never lands on a recycled pid.
- `ExitSelf` — a same-or-newer incumbent holds the socket; `errStepAside` flows out and `serve` swallows it for a clean exit 0.

`daemonPeer` (`internal/daemon/peer.go:27#nbxh`) adapts the frozen wire to daemonkit's `daemon.Peer` and reads replies skew-tolerantly: takeover only needs OK, Version, and Error across an upgrade skew, while public clients and work ops stay strict. Server-side, `OpHealth` and `OpShutdown` bypass the protocol-version gate and the drain (`internal/daemon/server.go:496#wraf`), so a draining or proto-skewed daemon still answers the takeover probe and a mid-drain Shutdown still lands. cc-pool advertises no `FeatureHandoff`: `Handoff` always errors, and eviction is the only takeover path.

## Drain: settle before cancel

`serve` splits its contexts: `drainCtx` (SIGINT/SIGTERM or `OpShutdown`) only stops intake, while `execCtx` (`context.WithoutCancel`) keeps admitted requests live through the settle and is cancelled last. `s.drain.Drain` runs Deactivate, settle, MarkClosing, then CancelExecutors (`internal/daemon/server.go:425#dmcp`). Work ops `Admit()` into the drain; once draining, new work is refused with "daemon draining". Shutdown acknowledgements are written before exit, because lifecycle handlers are tracked on `s.wg` and `serve` waits on it before returning. The sync socket sits inside the same drain: `admittedSyncConsumer` (`internal/daemon/syncserver.go:54#rv2p`) wraps every `SyncConsumer` method in an `Admit`/`done` pair.

## LaunchAgent policy: KeepAlive with SuccessfulExit false

The Homebrew service block sets `keep_alive successful_exit: false` (`.github/formula/cc-pool.rb.tmpl:195#nz6p`): launchd restarts a failed daemon but leaves a clean exit alone. That clean exit is precisely the step-aside path above, so a superseded daemon is not relaunched into a takeover loop. The self-managed plist enforces the same policy: `adaptCCPAgentPlist` rewrites daemonkit's default always-on `KeepAlive` stanza to the on-failure dict (`internal/cli/service.go:142#g6k4`, the `keepAliveOnFailure` constant) and errors when the expected daemonkit stanza is missing. The formula and the plist adapter must stay in lockstep; a change to one changes the other.

## Cancellation propagation

`Client.EnsureRunning` threads its context into `proc.Spawn` (`internal/daemon/spawn.go:11#f5r2`), and the service CLI's launchd and Homebrew waits run under the command context. Commands that start, stop, inspect, or wait for the daemon abort on cancellation instead of sleeping out their timeouts.

## Not adopted

- `daemonkit/trust` — cc-pool does not codesign-verify socket peers.
- `daemonkit/wire` — the custom JSON socket protocol (frozen `Request`/`Response`, the `ProtocolVersion` gate) is retained. Only the lifecycle ops are skew-tolerant; everything else rejects a protocol mismatch.
ops.when: when touching cc-pool daemon boot, takeover, drain, LaunchAgent/Homebrew service policy, or version stamping
